title: The Second Book of Kings Timeline
sub: Elisha's Miracles · The Fall of Israel and Judah
desc: Elijah is taken up in a whirlwind and Elisha inherits his mantle, working miracles across both kingdoms even as their kings spiral toward disaster: first Israel falls to Assyria, then Judah, after one last reforming king, falls to Babylon and the temple burns.

eras.label: Era One · 2 Kings 1
eras.name: Ahaziah Consults Baal Zebub, and Fire From Heaven
eras.dates: Injured and seeking a foreign oracle instead of Israel's own God, King Ahaziah of Israel gets a death sentence from Elijah instead, and two companies of soldiers sent to arrest the prophet are consumed by fire before a third captain simply begs for mercy.

events.title: "Is There No God in Israel?"
events.detail: Injured in a fall, Ahaziah sends to Baal Zebub of Ekron for a prognosis rather than to the LORD; the angel of the LORD intercepts his messengers through Elijah with a pointed rebuke and a death sentence.

verses.text: “The angel of the LORD [Yahweh] told Elijah the Tishbite, ‘Get up; go to meet the messengers… Say this to them: “You must think there is no God [Elohim] in Israel! That explains why you are on your way to seek an oracle from Baal Zebub the god [Elohim] of Ekron.”’”

events.title: Fire Consumes Two Captains; the Third Begs for Mercy
events.detail: Two companies of fifty sent to arrest Elijah are consumed by fire he calls down from the sky; a third captain falls on his knees pleading for his life instead of issuing orders, and Elijah is permitted to go down and deliver the same verdict to Ahaziah's face, who dies as declared, leaving no son, so his brother Jehoram succeeds him.

verses.text: “He said to him, ‘This is what the LORD [Yahweh] has said: because you have sent messengers to consult Baal Zebub the god [Elohim] of Ekron — is it because there is no God [Elohim] in Israel to consult his word? — therefore you will not come down from the bed where you have gone up, for you will surely die.’”

eras.label: Era Two · 2 Kings 2
eras.name: Elijah Taken Up; Elisha's Double Portion
eras.dates: Elijah's ministry ends in a whirlwind rather than a grave, and Elisha inherits both his cloak and his prophetic authority: proven immediately by dividing the Jordan, purifying a poisoned spring, and a curse on mocking boys that costs forty-two lives.

events.title: The Road to the Jordan
events.detail: Elijah repeatedly tells Elisha to stay behind at Bethel, then Jericho, then the Jordan, and each time Elisha refuses to leave him; at the Jordan, Elijah strikes the water with his rolled-up cloak and the two cross over on dry ground.

events.title: "A Double Portion of Your Spirit": the Whirlwind and the Cloak
events.detail: Elisha asks for a double portion of Elijah's prophetic spirit; a fiery chariot and horses suddenly separate the two, and Elijah goes up to heaven in a windstorm, leaving Elisha his cloak, which Elisha uses at once to strike and divide the Jordan himself, proving the spirit has passed to him.

verses.text: “He took the cloak of Elijah which had fallen from him and struck the waters and said, ‘Where is the LORD [Yahweh], the God [Elohim] of Elijah?’ He also struck the waters, and they were divided, and Elisha crossed over.”

events.title: Purified Water, and Bears for Mocking Boys
events.detail: The prophetic guild bows to Elisha as Elijah's successor; he purifies Jericho's bad spring with salt so it never causes death again, but when boys near Bethel mock him for his baldness, he curses them and two bears maul forty-two of them.

verses.text: “Then he said, ‘This is what the LORD has said: “I have purified this water. It will no longer cause death or fail to produce crops.”’”

eras.label: Era Three · 2 Kings 3
eras.name: Moab's Rebellion and the Water in the Desert
eras.dates: Moab's king stops paying tribute after Ahab's death, and an allied campaign against him nearly dies of thirst in the wilderness before Elisha promises water without wind or rain: followed by an atrocity that ends the campaign in horror rather than triumph.

events.title: Three Kings Run Out of Water
events.detail: Jehoram of Israel, allied with Jehoshaphat of Judah and the king of Edom, marches against rebelling Moab by a desert route and runs completely out of water for both men and animals, prompting a search for a true prophet of the LORD.

events.title: Elisha's Promise of Water, and Mesha's Child Sacrifice
events.detail: Elisha, respecting Jehoshaphat's presence rather than Jehoram's, promises the valley will fill with water though no wind or rain will be seen, and predicts total victory over Moab; when the campaign nonetheless fails to take Kir Hareseth, Moab's king sacrifices his own firstborn son on the wall, provoking such horror that the allied army withdraws.

verses.text: “You will not feel any wind or see any rain, but this valley will be full of water, and you and your cattle and animals will drink. This is an easy task for the LORD [Yahweh]; he will also hand Moab over to you.”

eras.label: Era Four · 2 Kings 4
eras.name: Elisha's Miracles — Oil, a Son, and a Poisoned Pot
eras.dates: A chain of domestic miracles (a widow's debt paid by oil that keeps flowing, a childless woman granted a son who later dies and is raised, a poisoned stew made safe, and a hundred men fed from twenty loaves) establishes Elisha as a wonder-worker on Elijah's own scale.

events.title: The Widow's Oil That Would Not Stop
events.detail: A prophet's widow, facing debt-slavery for her two sons, is told by Elisha to borrow empty jars and pour her one small jar of oil into them; it keeps flowing until every borrowed jar is full, providing enough to pay the debt and live on.

events.title: The Shunammite Woman Promised a Son
events.detail: A well-off woman in Shunem builds Elisha a private room whenever he passes through; in gratitude, he promises her a son within the year despite her husband's age: a promise fulfilled exactly on schedule.

verses.text: “He said, ‘About this time next year you will be holding a son.’ She said, ‘No, my master! O prophet, do not lie to your servant!’”

events.title: The Boy Dies, and Elisha Raises Him
events.detail: Years later the boy dies suddenly of what sounds like heatstroke; the Shunammite lays him on Elisha's bed and fetches the prophet, who stretches himself over the child's body twice before he sneezes seven times and opens his eyes.

verses.text: “He got up on the bed and spread his body out over the boy… As he bent down across him, the boy's skin grew warm.”
“He got up on the bed again and bent down over him. The child sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.”

events.title: Death in the Pot, and a Hundred Fed
events.detail: During a famine, wild gourds mistakenly cooked into the prophets' stew turn it poisonous until Elisha adds flour to neutralize it; shortly after, twenty loaves of barley bread feed a hundred men with food left over, exactly as Elisha had said.

verses.text: “His attendant said, ‘How can I feed a hundred men with this?’ He replied, ‘Set it before the people so they may eat, for this is what the LORD has said, “They will eat and have some left over.”’ So he set it before them; they ate and had some left over, just as in the LORD's message.”

eras.label: Era Five · 2 Kings 5
eras.name: Naaman Healed, and Gehazi's Greed
eras.dates: A foreign general's skin disease is healed by washing in the Jordan seven times, prompting his conversion, and a servant's secret greed for the reward Elisha refused transfers the disease onto himself and his descendants forever.

events.title: Naaman Washes Seven Times in the Jordan
events.detail: A captive Israelite girl points Naaman, commander of Syria's army, toward Elisha; offended that the prophet merely sends word to wash seven times in the Jordan rather than appearing with dramatic ritual, Naaman nearly leaves angry, but his servants talk him into obeying, and his skin becomes like a child's.

verses.text: “He went down and dipped in the Jordan seven times, as the prophet had instructed. His skin became as smooth as a young child's and he was healed.”

events.title: "There Is No God in All the Earth Except in Israel": and Gehazi's Curse
events.detail: Naaman confesses the LORD alone is God and asks forgiveness in advance for the compromises his court position will require; Elisha refuses any payment, but his servant Gehazi secretly chases Naaman down for silver and clothes, and inherits Naaman's skin disease as his reward instead.

verses.text: “He said, ‘Here, please — I know that there is no God [Elohim] in all the earth except in Israel! Now, please accept a blessing from your servant.’”
“‘Therefore Naaman's skin disease will afflict you and your descendants forever!’ When Gehazi went out from his presence, his skin was as white as snow.”

eras.label: Era Six · 2 Kings 6
eras.name: A Floating Axhead, Blinded Raiders, and a City Under Siege
eras.dates: Elisha's power ranges from the domestic (a borrowed axhead recovered) to the strategic (a Syrian army struck blind and led into Samaria) to the horrifying (a siege so severe that two mothers agree to eat their sons).

events.title: The Floating Axhead
events.detail: When a borrowed iron axhead sinks into the Jordan during a building project, Elisha throws in a stick and makes the iron float back to the surface.

events.title: The Chariots of Fire, and a Blinded Army Fed Instead of Killed
events.detail: Elisha repeatedly warns the king of Israel of Syrian ambush locations, frustrating Syria's king until he sends an army to capture the prophet himself; Elisha's servant sees a hillside full of fiery chariots invisible to him until Elisha prays his eyes open, and the approaching Syrian force is struck blind, led into Samaria, fed a banquet, and sent home instead of killed.

verses.text: “Elisha prayed, ‘O LORD [Yahweh], open his eyes so he can see.’ The LORD [Yahweh] opened the servant's eyes, and he saw that the hill was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.”

events.title: Siege, Famine, and Cannibalism in Samaria
events.detail: Ben Hadad's full siege of Samaria drives food prices to grotesque extremes; when a starving mother reports that she and another woman boiled and ate her son, as agreed, but the second woman then hid her own son rather than delivering him, the horrified king vows to execute Elisha for the disaster.

verses.text: “The king asked her, ‘What's your problem?’ She answered, ‘This woman said to me, “Hand over your son; we'll eat him today and then eat my son tomorrow.” So we boiled my son and ate him. Then I said to her the next day, “Hand over your son and we'll eat him.” But she hid her son!’”

eras.label: Era Seven · 2 Kings 7
eras.name: Four Lepers Discover an Abandoned Camp
eras.dates: Elisha promises overnight relief from the famine prices, a skeptical officer doubts it aloud, and four desperate outcasts stumble onto a Syrian camp the LORD emptied by the mere sound of a phantom army, fulfilling both promise and warning within a single day.

events.title: Four Men With Skin Disease Find an Empty Camp
events.detail: Elisha promises famine prices will collapse within a day; four men with a skin disease, reasoning they have nothing to lose, defect to the Syrian camp at dusk and find it completely abandoned: the LORD had made the Syrians hear the sound of a massive advancing army and they fled everything behind.

verses.text: “The LORD had caused the Syrian camp to hear the sound of chariots and horses and a large army. Then they said to one another, ‘Look, the king of Israel has paid the kings of the Hittites and Egyptians to attack us!’”

events.title: The Skeptical Officer Trampled at the Gate
events.detail: The king's own right-hand man, who had scoffed that Elisha's prophecy could not happen so fast, is trampled to death in the gate by the crowd rushing to loot the abandoned camp, dying without tasting the abundance he doubted, exactly as Elisha had told him.

verses.text: “An officer who was the king's right-hand man responded to the prophet, ‘Look, even if the LORD made it rain by opening holes in the sky, could this happen so soon?’ Elisha said, ‘Look, you will see it happen with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of the food!’… This is exactly what happened to him. The people trampled him to death in the city gate.”

eras.label: Era Eight · 2 Kings 8
eras.name: The Shunammite's Land, Hazael's Coup, and Judah's Ahab-Like Kings
eras.dates: The Shunammite woman's testimony before the king restores her land, Elisha weeps over what Hazael will do to Israel even as he foretells Hazael's kingship, and Judah's own royal line becomes entangled with Ahab's dynasty by marriage.

events.title: The Shunammite's Land Restored
events.detail: Returning from seven years in Philistine territory during a famine, the woman whose son Elisha raised petitions the king for her house and field, and by providential timing, arrives just as Gehazi is telling the king that very story, securing full restoration on the spot.

events.title: Hazael Murders Ben Hadad
events.detail: Elisha weeps while telling Hazael the atrocities he will commit against Israel as its future king, then tells him plainly the LORD has revealed he will indeed be king; Hazael returns and smothers the sick Ben Hadad with a wet cloth the next day, taking the throne.

verses.text: “He replied, ‘Because I know the trouble you will cause the Israelites. You will set fire to their fortresses, kill their young men with the sword, smash their children to bits, and rip open their pregnant women.’ Hazael said, ‘How could your servant… accomplish this great military victory?’ Elisha answered, ‘The LORD has revealed to me that you will be the king of Syria.’”

events.title: Jehoram and Ahaziah of Judah: Ahab's Dynasty by Marriage
events.detail: Judah's king Jehoram marries Ahab's daughter and follows Israel's kings into evil, yet the LORD preserves Judah for David's sake; his son Ahaziah, related to Ahab's house through his mother Athaliah, allies with Israel's King Joram against Syria at Ramoth Gilead, where Joram is wounded and Ahaziah goes to visit him at Jezreel.

verses.text: “But the LORD was unwilling to destroy Judah. He preserved Judah for the sake of his servant David to whom he had promised a perpetual dynasty.”

eras.label: Era Nine · 2 Kings 9
eras.name: Jehu Anointed — the Deaths of Joram, Ahaziah, and Jezebel
eras.dates: Elisha's secret anointing of Jehu triggers a violent purge that begins within the same chapter: Joram shot through the heart at Naboth's own plot of land, Ahaziah cut down in flight, and Jezebel thrown from a window to be eaten by dogs.

events.title: Jehu Secretly Anointed King
events.detail: A young prophet sent by Elisha anoints Jehu in a private room and declares his commission to destroy Ahab's entire house in vengeance for the LORD's murdered prophets and servants, then flees before Jehu's fellow officers proclaim him king on the spot.

verses.text: “He poured the oil on his head and said to him, ‘This is what the LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of Israel has said: “I have designated you as king over the LORD's [Yahweh] people Israel. You will destroy the family of your master Ahab. I will get revenge against Jezebel for the shed blood of my servants the prophets.”’”

events.title: Joram Shot at Naboth's Plot; Ahaziah Cut Down
events.detail: Jehu drives recklessly to Jezreel and shoots Joram through the heart with an arrow at the exact plot of land once stolen from Naboth, explicitly fulfilling Elijah's old oracle against Ahab's house, then chases down and mortally wounds the fleeing Ahaziah of Judah as well.

verses.text: “‘Know for sure that I saw the shed blood of Naboth and his sons yesterday,’ says the LORD [Yahweh], ‘and that I will give you what you deserve right here in this plot of land,’ says the LORD [Yahweh]. So now pick him up and throw him into this plot of land, just as in the LORD's message.”

events.title: Jezebel Thrown From the Window
events.detail: Jezebel paints her eyes and taunts Jehu from a window as he arrives; at his command her own eunuchs throw her down, and by the time anyone goes to bury her body, dogs have already devoured all but her skull, feet, and palms: exactly as Elijah had prophesied years before.

verses.text: “He said, ‘It is the fulfillment of the LORD's message that he had spoken through his servant, Elijah the Tishbite, “In the plot of land at Jezreel, dogs will devour Jezebel's flesh. Jezebel's corpse will be like manure on the surface of the ground.”’”

eras.label: Era Ten · 2 Kings 10
eras.name: Jehu's Purge, and the Sin He Kept
eras.dates: Jehu wipes out every remaining member of Ahab's house and every priest of Baal in Israel with ruthless efficiency, yet keeps Jeroboam's golden calves standing at Bethel and Dan: a half-obedience the narrative refuses to let pass as full loyalty.

events.title: Seventy Heads in Baskets
events.detail: Jehu forces Samaria's leading men to execute all seventy of Ahab's royal sons and send their heads to Jezreel in baskets, then kills every remaining relative, noble, priest, and friend of Ahab's house: publicly declaring that not one of the LORD's words against that dynasty will fail.

verses.text: “Take note that not one of the LORD's [Yahweh] words which he pronounced against Ahab's dynasty will fail to materialize. The LORD [Yahweh] has done what he announced through his servant Elijah.”

events.title: The Temple of Baal Destroyed
events.detail: Jehu tricks all of Baal's priests and worshipers into a single assembly under the pretense of a great sacrifice, then has them slaughtered and the temple of Baal itself demolished and turned into a latrine, eradicating organized Baal worship from Israel.

events.title: "You Have Done Well": But the Calves Remain
events.detail: The LORD commends Jehu's zeal against Ahab's house with a promise of four generations on Israel's throne, yet the narrator notes flatly that Jehu never tore down Jeroboam's golden calves: an incomplete reform that leaves Israel's core sin untouched even as its borders begin shrinking under Hazael's attacks.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] said to Jehu, ‘You have done well… Therefore four generations of your descendants will rule over Israel.’ But Jehu did not carefully and wholeheartedly obey the law of the LORD God of Israel. He did not repudiate the sins which Jeroboam had encouraged Israel to commit.”

eras.label: Era Eleven · 2 Kings 11
eras.name: Athaliah's Massacre, and the Hidden King
eras.dates: Ahaziah's mother Athaliah tries to exterminate the entire Davidic royal line to secure her own throne, but a baby prince is smuggled away and hidden in the temple for six years before a priest-led coup restores him and puts Athaliah to death.

events.title: Athaliah Seizes the Throne; Joash Hidden
events.detail: When Athaliah learns her son Ahaziah is dead, she moves to destroy the entire royal family to secure the throne for herself, but Jehosheba smuggles the infant Joash away and hides him in the LORD's temple for six years while Athaliah rules.

events.title: Jehoiada's Coup: Joash Crowned
events.detail: In the seventh year, the priest Jehoiada arms the temple guard, presents the hidden boy-king, crowns him, and anoints him amid the people's shouts of "Long live the king!"

events.title: "Treason!": Athaliah's Death and Covenant Renewal
events.detail: Athaliah is dragged out of the temple to be executed rather than desecrating it with her death; the temple of Baal is torn down and its priest killed, and Jehoiada draws up a covenant between the LORD, the king, and the people, restoring the city to rest and rightful worship.

verses.text: “Jehoiada then drew up a covenant between the LORD [Yahweh] and the king and people, stipulating that they should be loyal to the LORD [Yahweh].”

eras.label: Era Twelve · 2 Kings 12
eras.name: Jehoash Repairs the Temple, and Buys Off Hazael
eras.dates: The boy-king raised under Jehoiada's tutelage institutes a working system to fund temple repairs, but ends his reign stripping that same temple's treasuries to bribe Hazael away from Jerusalem, and dies at the hands of his own conspiring servants. (Hebrew chapter 12 begins with the verse most English Bibles number as 11:21.)

events.title: Jehoash Orders Temple Repairs
events.detail: Jehoash, doing what was right under Jehoiada's teaching, orders the priests to use consecrated silver for repairing the temple, but by his twenty-third year the repairs still haven't happened, and he sharply rebukes them for the delay.

events.title: The Chest by the Altar
events.detail: Jehoiada institutes a simple, accountable system, a chest with a hole in the lid by the altar, that finally gets the silver collected and paid directly to honest foremen and craftsmen for the temple's repair.

events.title: Hazael Bought Off; Jehoash Assassinated
events.detail: Rather than fight off Hazael's advance on Jerusalem, Jehoash strips every sacred and treasury item he can find, including his own ancestors' dedications, and sends it all as tribute; not long after, his own servants conspire against him and murder him, and his son Amaziah succeeds him.

verses.text: “He sent it all to King Hazael of Syria, who then withdrew from Jerusalem.”

eras.label: Era Thirteen · 2 Kings 13
eras.name: Jehoahaz, Jehoash, and the Death of Elisha
eras.dates: Two kings named Jehoahaz and Jehoash suffer and then recover from Syrian oppression under the LORD's mercy, and the book pauses for Elisha's death scene, including a final symbolic act, and one more miracle performed from inside his own tomb.

events.title: Jehoahaz Oppressed, Then Delivered
events.detail: Jehoahaz's continuation of Jeroboam's sins brings Syrian oppression so severe his army is reduced to a token force, but when he pleads for the LORD's mercy, a deliverer is provided and Israel regains security.

verses.text: “Jehoahaz asked for the LORD's mercy, and the LORD responded favorably, for he saw that Israel was oppressed by the king of Syria. The LORD provided a deliverer for Israel, and they were freed from Syria's power.”

events.title: Elisha's Final Act: Arrows of Victory
events.detail: On his deathbed, Elisha has King Jehoash shoot an arrow through an open window as a symbol of victory over Syria, then has him strike the ground with the remaining arrows; Jehoash stops after only three halfhearted strikes, and an angry Elisha limits Israel's coming victories over Syria to three instead of the total defeat five or six strikes would have secured.

verses.text: “The prophet got angry at him and said, ‘If you had struck the ground five or six times, you would have annihilated Syria! But now, you will defeat Syria only three times.’”

events.title: A Miracle From the Grave
events.detail: Elisha dies and is buried, but when a corpse hastily thrown into his tomb touches his bones, the dead man springs back to life: a final sign of the power that had rested on the prophet even beyond death, as Jehoash goes on to recover Israelite cities from Syria three times.

verses.text: “When the body touched Elisha's bones, the dead man came to life and stood on his feet.”

eras.label: Era Fourteen · 2 Kings 14
eras.name: Amaziah's War With Israel, and Jeroboam II's Restoration
eras.dates: Amaziah of Judah's pride after defeating Edom draws him into a humiliating war with Israel, while in the north Jeroboam II restores Israel's borders to their widest extent since Solomon: through an otherwise obscure prophet named Jonah.

events.title: Amaziah's Partial Obedience, and Victory Over Edom
events.detail: Amaziah does what is right but leaves the high places standing, executes his father's assassins but spares their sons in explicit obedience to the law of Moses, and defeats 10,000 Edomites, renaming the captured city Joktheel.

verses.text: “He obeyed the LORD's commandment as recorded in the scroll of the law of Moses, ‘Fathers must not be put to death for what their sons do, and sons must not be put to death for what their fathers do. A man must be put to death only for his own sin.’”

events.title: The Thornbush and the Cedar: Judah Humiliated
events.detail: Flush with victory, Amaziah challenges Israel's Jehoash to battle; Jehoash's parable comparing Amaziah to a thornbush trampled by a wild animal proves prophetic: Judah is routed, Jerusalem's wall broken down, and the temple and palace treasuries plundered.

verses.text: “King Jehoash of Israel sent this message back to King Amaziah of Judah, ‘A thornbush in Lebanon sent this message to a cedar in Lebanon, “Give your daughter to my son as a wife.” Then a wild animal of Lebanon came by and trampled down the thorn.’”

events.title: Jeroboam II Restores Israel's Borders: Through Jonah's Word
events.detail: Despite Jeroboam II's continuation of Jeroboam I's sins, the LORD has mercy on suffering Israel and restores its borders to nearly Solomonic extent, explicitly fulfilling a word spoken through the prophet Jonah son of Amittai: the same Jonah of the book that bears his name.

verses.text: “He restored the border of Israel from Lebo Hamath in the north to the sea of the rift valley in the south, just as in the message from the LORD God of Israel that he had announced through his servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath Hepher.”

eras.label: Era Fifteen · 2 Kings 15
eras.name: A Cascade of Kings — Assassination After Assassination in Israel
eras.dates: While Judah's Azariah and Jotham enjoy long, stable reigns, Israel's throne changes hands violently five times in a single chapter (Zechariah, Shallum, Menahem, Pekahiah, and Pekah) as Assyria's shadow begins falling over the northern kingdom.

events.title: Azariah's Fifty-Two Years, and a Skin Disease
events.detail: Azariah (Uzziah) reigns for fifty-two years doing what is right, though the LORD afflicts him with a skin disease that confines him to separate quarters for the rest of his life while his son Jotham governs in his place.

events.title: Zechariah, Shallum, Menahem, Pekahiah, Pekah: the Fourth Generation Ends
events.detail: Zechariah's six-month reign and assassination by Shallum fulfills the LORD's word to Jehu that only four generations of his line would hold the throne; Shallum himself is killed within a month by Menahem, whose brutal conquest of Tiphsah rips open pregnant women; Menahem's son Pekahiah is assassinated by his own officer Pekah, who then loses swaths of northern territory to Assyria's Tiglath-Pileser.

verses.text: “His assassination fulfilled the LORD's message to Jehu, ‘Four generations of your descendants will rule on Israel's throne.’ And that is how it happened.”

“During Pekah's reign over Israel, King Tiglath-Pileser of Assyria came and captured Ijon, Abel Beth Maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee, including all the territory of Naphtali. He deported the people to Assyria.”

events.title: Jotham of Judah
events.detail: Jotham reigns sixteen years doing what was right like his father, building the temple's Upper Gate, even as the LORD begins prompting Syria and Israel's Pekah to move against Judah in the events that will define the next chapter.

eras.label: Era Sixteen · 2 Kings 16
eras.name: Ahaz — Vassalage to Assyria, and a Borrowed Altar
eras.dates: Besieged by Syria and Israel together, Ahaz buys Assyrian rescue with the temple's own treasures, then commissions a new altar copied from one he admired in Damascus and rearranges the temple's furnishings to suit his foreign patron.

events.title: Ahaz Buys Assyrian Help
events.detail: Under siege from Syria and Israel and practicing child sacrifice himself, Ahaz strips the temple and palace treasuries to buy King Tiglath-Pileser of Assyria's intervention, formally submitting as his "servant and dependent."

verses.text: “Ahaz sent messengers to King Tiglath-Pileser of Assyria, saying, ‘I am your servant and your dependent. March up and rescue me from the power of the king of Syria and the king of Israel, who have attacked me.’”

events.title: A New Altar Copied From Damascus
events.detail: Impressed by an altar he saw in Damascus, Ahaz sends the design home and has Uriah the priest build a replica in the temple, displacing the bronze altar to secondary use and rearranging other temple furnishings to accommodate his new arrangement, on account of the king of Assyria.

eras.label: Era Seventeen · 2 Kings 17
eras.name: The Fall of Samaria — Israel's Exile Explained
eras.dates: Assyria finally conquers Samaria and deports the northern kingdom for good, and the narrator pauses the chronicle for an extended theological explanation: exile as the direct consequence of generations of idolatry despite repeated prophetic warning.

events.title: Samaria Falls; Israel Deported
events.detail: Hoshea's attempted revolt against Assyria, seeking Egyptian help instead of paying tribute, brings a three-year siege that ends with Samaria's capture and the deportation of Israel's population to Assyrian territory, ending the northern kingdom.

events.title: Why It Happened: a Theological Verdict
events.detail: The narrator explains the exile at length: Israel worshiped other gods, built high places everywhere, ignored every prophetic warning, and imitated the very nations the LORD had driven out, so the LORD rejected Israel just as he had warned, tearing the ten tribes away from David's line ever since Jeroboam first led them astray.

verses.text: “It was because the people of Israel had sinned against the LORD [Yahweh] their God [Elohim], who brought them up from the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they had feared other gods [Elohim].”
“Finally the LORD rejected Israel just as he had warned he would do through all his servants the prophets. Israel was deported from its land to Assyria and remains there to this very day.”

events.title: Resettlement and a Syncretistic Worship
events.detail: Assyria resettles foreign peoples in Samaria's cities, who initially ignore the local God until lions begin killing them; a deported priest is sent back to teach them to "worship the LORD," but the resulting religion blends LORD-worship with each nation's own gods: a pattern the narrator notes persists "to this very day."

verses.text: “Instead you must worship the LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim]; then he will rescue you from the power of all your enemies.”

eras.label: Era Eighteen · 2 Kings 18
eras.name: Hezekiah's Reforms, and Sennacherib's Threat
eras.dates: Hezekiah tears down every high place (even Moses's own bronze serpent, which had become an idol) and trusts the LORD so completely that he rebels against Assyria outright, drawing Sennacherib's army and a chief adviser's blistering public taunt to Jerusalem's very walls.

events.title: Hezekiah Eliminates the High Places: Even Nehushtan
events.detail: Unlike any king before or after, Hezekiah trusts the LORD completely, destroying the high places, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles, and even demolishing the bronze serpent Moses made in the wilderness because the Israelites had turned it into an idol called Nehushtan.

verses.text: “He also demolished the bronze serpent that Moses had made, for up to that time the Israelites had been offering incense to it… He trusted in the LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of Israel; in this regard there was none like him among the kings of Judah either before or after.”

events.title: The Rabshakeh's Taunt at the Walls
events.detail: Sennacherib's army captures Judah's fortified cities and demands crushing tribute; even after Hezekiah pays it, the Assyrian chief adviser publicly mocks Judah's trust in the LORD before the people on the wall, calling it as empty as trust in "a splintered reed staff" of Egypt, and openly claiming the LORD himself sent Assyria to destroy Jerusalem.

verses.text: “‘Perhaps you will tell me, “We are trusting in the LORD our God.”’ But Hezekiah is the one who eliminated his high places and altars and then told the people of Judah and Jerusalem, ‘You must worship at this altar in Jerusalem.’”
“‘Who among all the gods of the lands has rescued their lands from my power? So how can the LORD rescue Jerusalem from my power?’”

eras.label: Era Nineteen · 2 Kings 19
eras.name: Hezekiah's Prayer, and the Angel of the LORD
eras.dates: Hezekiah spreads Sennacherib's taunting letter before the LORD in the temple, and Isaiah answers with a detailed oracle of Assyria's defeat: fulfilled that very night when the angel of the LORD kills 185,000 troops and Sennacherib is assassinated by his own sons.

events.title: Hezekiah Seeks Isaiah; Sennacherib Taunts Again
events.detail: Hezekiah tears his clothes and sends to Isaiah for a word from the LORD; Isaiah promises Sennacherib will hear a report and return home to die by the sword, but Sennacherib sends a second letter mocking every god that failed to save other nations from Assyria, daring Hezekiah's God to be any different.

events.title: Hezekiah Spreads the Letter Before the LORD
events.detail: Hezekiah takes Sennacherib's taunting letter into the temple and spreads it out before the LORD in prayer, appealing to God's uniqueness over every false god of wood and stone and asking deliverance so that "all the kingdoms of the earth will know that you, LORD, are the only God."

verses.text: “Hezekiah prayed before the LORD [Yahweh] and said, ‘O LORD [Yahweh], God [Elohim] of Israel, who is enthroned above the cherubim! You alone are God [Elohim] over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the sky and the earth.’”
“‘Now, O LORD [Yahweh] our God [Elohim], rescue us from his power, so that all the kingdoms of the earth will know that you, LORD [Yahweh], are the only God [Elohim].’”

events.title: Isaiah's Oracle, and 185,000 Struck Down in a Night
events.detail: Isaiah delivers a taunting poem against Sennacherib in the LORD's own voice, promising to "put my hook in your nose" and send him home the way he came; that same night the angel of the LORD kills 185,000 men in the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib himself is later murdered by his own sons while worshiping his god Nisroch.

verses.text: “‘I will defend this city to deliver it, for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.’”
“That very night the angel of the LORD went out and killed 185,000 in the Assyrian camp. When they got up early the next morning, there were all the corpses.”

eras.label: Era Twenty · 2 Kings 20
eras.name: Hezekiah's Illness, the Sundial Sign, and Babylon's Envoys
eras.dates: Hezekiah's tearful prayer against a terminal diagnosis earns him fifteen more years and a sign of the sun's shadow reversing course, but showing off his wealth to Babylonian envoys draws Isaiah's warning that everything he displayed will one day be carried off to that very kingdom.

events.title: "I Will Add Fifteen Years to Your Life"
events.detail: Told by Isaiah to prepare for death, Hezekiah weeps and prays, reminding the LORD of his wholehearted devotion; before Isaiah has even left the courtyard, the LORD sends him back with healing, fifteen additional years, and a confirming sign: the sun's shadow moving backward ten steps on the stairway of Ahaz.

verses.text: “‘This is what the LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of your ancestor David has said: “I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Look, I will heal you… I will add fifteen years to your life.”’”

events.title: Babylon's Envoys, and a Warning of Exile
events.detail: Hezekiah proudly shows Babylonian envoys every treasure in his kingdom; Isaiah's response is a stark warning that everything displayed, and some of Hezekiah's own descendants, will one day be carried off to Babylon, a warning Hezekiah accepts only because it means peace during his own lifetime.

verses.text: “‘Look, a time is coming when everything in your palace and the things your ancestors have accumulated to this day will be carried away to Babylon; nothing will be left,’ says the LORD.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-One · 2 Kings 21
eras.name: Manasseh's Apostasy, and Amon's Brief Reign
eras.dates: Hezekiah's reforming son gives way to Manasseh, whose fifty-five-year reign rebuilds every high place his father tore down and fills Jerusalem with innocent blood: sins the narrative treats as the true, irreversible cause of Judah's coming destruction.

events.title: Manasseh Rebuilds Every High Place
events.detail: Manasseh systematically undoes his father's reforms, rebuilding high places, erecting altars to Baal and the stars even inside the LORD's own temple, practicing child sacrifice and divination, and misleading Judah into sinning "more than the nations" the LORD had destroyed before them.

verses.text: “He passed his son through the fire and practiced divination and omen reading. He set up a ritual pit to conjure up underworld spirits… He did a great amount of evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking him to anger.”

events.title: "I Will Wipe Jerusalem Clean, as One Wipes a Plate"
events.detail: The LORD announces through his prophets that disaster is now certain for Jerusalem and Judah, measured by the same standard applied to Samaria and Ahab's dynasty, because of Manasseh's sins and the innocent blood he shed "from end to end" of the city.

verses.text: “Thus says the LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of Israel, ‘I am about to bring disaster on Jerusalem and Judah… I will wipe Jerusalem clean, just as one wipes a plate on both sides.’”

events.title: Amon's Two Years, and Josiah's Accession
events.detail: Manasseh's son Amon continues his father's idolatry for just two years before his own servants assassinate him; the people of the land execute the conspirators and crown his young son Josiah in his place.

eras.label: Era Twenty-Two · 2 Kings 22
eras.name: Josiah, the Scroll of the Law, and Huldah's Oracle
eras.dates: A temple repair project turns up a forgotten scroll of the law, and Josiah's reaction, torn clothes and genuine terror at how far Judah has strayed, sends his officials to the prophetess Huldah, who confirms disaster is coming but grants Josiah himself a peaceful death before it arrives.

events.title: Repairing the Temple
events.detail: In his eighteenth year, Josiah orders temple repairs funded by silver collected from the people, instructing that the honest foremen overseeing the work not even be audited.

events.title: The Scroll of the Law Is Found
events.detail: Hilkiah the high priest discovers "the scroll of the law" during the repairs; when it is read aloud to Josiah, he tears his clothes in genuine alarm at how completely Judah has failed to obey what it contains, and sends his officials to seek a prophetic word about it.

verses.text: “‘Go, seek an oracle from the LORD for me and the people—for all Judah. Find out about the words of this scroll that has been discovered. For the LORD's great fury has been ignited against us, because our ancestors have not obeyed the words of this scroll.’”

events.title: Huldah's Oracle: Disaster Coming, but Not in Josiah's Lifetime
events.detail: The prophetess Huldah confirms that the disaster written in the scroll will indeed come upon Jerusalem for its idolatry, but because Josiah's heart was soft and he humbled himself when he heard it, she promises he will die in peace before he has to witness it.

verses.text: “‘Because your heart was soft and you humbled yourself before the LORD [Yahweh]… therefore I will allow you to die and be buried in peace. You will not have to witness all the disaster I will bring on this place.’”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Three · 2 Kings 23
eras.name: Josiah's Reforms and Passover, and His Death at Megiddo
eras.dates: Josiah leads the most sweeping religious reform of any king in either kingdom's history (purging the temple, desecrating rival altars as far back as Solomon's own high places, and reviving a Passover unseen since the days of the judges) yet dies suddenly in battle against Pharaoh Necho, and Judah's final decline resumes almost immediately.

events.title: The Covenant Renewed and Idolatry Purged
events.detail: Josiah reads the scroll publicly and renews the covenant before the LORD with the full assembly's agreement, then systematically destroys every trace of Baal, Asherah, and astral worship in the temple and its precincts, tearing down even Solomon's own centuries-old high places to Astarte, Chemosh, and Milcom.

verses.text: “The king stood by the pillar and renewed the covenant before the LORD and to obey his commandments, laws, and rules with all his heart and being.”

events.title: The Altar at Bethel Defiled: an Old Prophecy Fulfilled
events.detail: Josiah defiles the altar at Bethel by burning human bones on it, fulfilling the centuries-old prophecy of the unnamed man of God from Judah in the days of Jeroboam I, and specifically spares the grave of that prophet and the old prophet buried beside him.

verses.text: “So he ordered the bones from the tombs to be brought; he burned them on the altar and defiled it, just as in the LORD's message that was announced by the prophet… ‘It's the grave of the prophet who came from Judah and foretold these very things you have done to the altar of Bethel.’”

events.title: A Passover Like No Other, but Judgment Still Stands
events.detail: Josiah's Passover surpasses anything celebrated since the era of the judges, and no king before or after repents as completely as he does, yet the narrator insists the LORD's anger over Manasseh's sins does not subside, and Jerusalem's fate remains sealed regardless.

verses.text: “Like him there had not been before him a king who turned back to the LORD [Yahweh] with all his heart and with all his being and with all his strength, according to all the law of Moses, and after him none arose like him.”

events.title: Josiah's Death at Megiddo
events.detail: Josiah is killed intercepting Pharaoh Necho's army at Megiddo; the people crown his son Jehoahaz, but Necho quickly deposes him for the more compliant Jehoiakim, who taxes the land heavily to pay Egypt's tribute.

verses.text: “During Josiah's reign Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt marched toward the Euphrates River to help the king of Assyria. King Josiah marched out to fight him, but Necho killed him at Megiddo when he saw him.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Four · 2 Kings 24
eras.name: Babylon Rises — Jehoiakim's Rebellion and the First Deportation
eras.dates: Babylon replaces Assyria and Egypt as the great power pressing on Judah, and Jehoiakim's rebellion against Nebuchadnezzar brings the first major deportation, including the young King Jehoiachin, ten thousand of Jerusalem's elite, and nearly every craftsman left in the city.

events.title: Jehoiakim Rebels Against Babylon
events.detail: Jehoiakim serves Nebuchadnezzar for three years before rebelling; raiding bands the LORD sends against him are explicitly tied to Manasseh's old sins, and Egypt's power in the region ends permanently as Babylon absorbs its former territory.

verses.text: “Just as the LORD had announced, he rejected Judah because of all the sins that Manasseh had committed. Because he killed innocent people and stained Jerusalem with their blood, the LORD was unwilling to forgive them.”

events.title: Jehoiachin Surrenders: the First Deportation
events.detail: The eighteen-year-old Jehoiachin surrenders to Nebuchadnezzar after only three months on the throne; the king of Babylon strips the temple treasuries, deports Jehoiachin along with ten thousand officials, soldiers, and craftsmen to Babylon, and installs his uncle Zedekiah as a puppet king who will himself rebel.

verses.text: “He deported all the residents of Jerusalem, including all the officials and all the soldiers (10,000 people in all). This included all the craftsmen and those who worked with metal. No one was left except for the poorest among the people of the land.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Five · 2 Kings 25
eras.name: The Fall of Jerusalem, and Jehoiachin's Release
eras.dates: Zedekiah's rebellion brings a two-year siege that ends in famine, a failed escape, the execution of the royal sons before their father's eyes, and the temple's destruction, but the book's very last scene is a small mercy, a pardoned king eating at a foreign table for the rest of his life.

events.title: Siege, Famine, and Zedekiah's Capture
events.detail: Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem for over a year until famine breaks the city; Zedekiah and his soldiers try to flee by night but are caught near Jericho, and Zedekiah is forced to watch his own sons executed before his eyes are put out and he is bound for Babylon.

verses.text: “Zedekiah's sons were executed while Zedekiah was forced to watch. The king of Babylon then had Zedekiah's eyes put out, bound him in bronze chains, and carried him off to Babylon.”

events.title: The Temple Burned, and Jerusalem's Walls Torn Down
events.detail: A month later, Nebuzaradan burns down the LORD's temple, the royal palace, and every great house in Jerusalem, tears down the city walls, and carries off or destroys every bronze and precious-metal furnishing Solomon had made (the two pillars, the movable stands, and the Sea itself) before Judah's remaining leaders are executed at Riblah.

verses.text: “He burned down the LORD's [Yahweh] temple, the royal palace, and all the houses in Jerusalem, including every large house.”

events.title: Gedaliah's Murder, and Jehoiachin's Pardon
events.detail: The governor Gedaliah, appointed over those left in the land, is assassinated within months by a royal-family conspirator, sending the remaining population fleeing to Egypt in fear, but the book's final scene shifts to Babylon, where a new king pardons the long-exiled Jehoiachin and gives him a seat of honor and provisions for the rest of his life.

verses.text: “Jehoiachin took off his prison clothes and ate daily in the king's presence for the rest of his life. He was given daily provisions by the king for the rest of his life until the day he died.”
